newsitem.title: HONG KONG: You are writing history, HK leadership panel told.
newsitem.headline: You are writing history, HK leadership panel told.

text.p: The panel of elite selectors assembled by China to choose Hong Kong's governor-in-waiting on Wednesday were told that they were writing history.

The 400 members, all carefully vetted by Beijing, were to select the man who will step into Governor Chris Patten's shoes when Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, is handed over to China at midnight on June 30 next year.

"You are writing the history of Hong Kong. I hope that you will cast your vote with a sense of responsibility to history, living up to the trust of the people of all China including Hong Kong," China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen told the electoral college before the ballots were distributed.
"I believe if Hong Kong is to be ruled by its own people, then the wishes of the people of Hong Kong must be respected.

"This is the position of the Central Government," said Qian, who made his second visit to Hong Kong to preside over the occasion, one of the most important milestones in the British colony's long and often bumpy transition.
Three candidates were vying for the historic post, but shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, 59, whose family empire was bailed out by China a decade ago, was expected to sweep effortlessly to victory.

Shanghai-born Tung grabbed 206 votes in the first round of voting last month. His nearest rival, former chief justice Yang Ti Liang, received 82 votes and the other leading contender, businessman Peter Woo, received 54.
Journalists were ejected from the hall while the ballots were distributed.
Pro-democracy activists, who have denounced the vote as a travesty of democracy and have boycotted the process, demonstrated outside the hall where the delegates had gathered.
